notes.title: [1.7] Main story improved, better quest journal, harder boss fights
notes.content:
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44662009/8a64b4bc944325b9d6c19a5a81651221147582e1.png[/img]
Hello everyone! ːsteamhappyː

Over the past month, I've focused on improving the writing in the main story—particularly the conflict between the orcs and elves, which now has a much stronger narrative foundation. While there haven't been any changes to gameplay or maps, the lore behind many of the main characters involved in the Stone quest has been updated. Most notably, the final boss now has a richer backstory, and the preceding bosses in the third act are more meaningfully connected to the overarching plot.

I also had the chance to watch Peaches stream the game on Twitch, which was incredibly valuable for identifying areas that still need balancing. One standout issue was how powerful parrying and backstabbing bosses can be. To address this, bosses are now more likely to counterattack when a backstab is attempted.

The Quest UI has been overhauled as well. It now provides much more visual information about objectives, their locations, and related characters. Players can now track multiple objectives at once, making questing smoother and more intuitive.

The game's intro has also changed—Cacildes now receives the king’s letter right from the start, making the chicken quest optional. This really opens up the game early on, allowing players to explore more freely without feeling locked into the first main quest area.

Here’s the full changelog:
[list]
[*] Rewrote the Stone and Molok storyline with stronger dialogue and deeper character motivations. Redesigned aspects of the main quest and the Forest Wanderers faction.
[*] Added a poison barrel minigame to the Lenny boss fight.
[*] Improved enemy sight behavior and gave some enemies the ability to jump.
[*] Revamped the following boss fights: Duo Orcs, Balbino, and Drogo – they now feature new attacks and increased difficulty.
[*] Bosses now counter backstabs more often – thanks to Peaches for pointing out this exploit!
[*] Made Käyro’s fight in the Elven Village more challenging by switching his weapons to shields. The Tombstone Shield now drops here, and his original spell can be found in a nearby chest.
[*] Increased the difficulty of the Celes and Molok boss fights; added a Vael’Noor statue puzzle to assist with the Celes fight.
[*] Added two new main story endings and expanded the epilogue.
[*] Overhauled the Quest Journal with detailed objectives, character bios, and trivia. You can now track multiple quests simultaneously.
[*] Added a cutscene with a camera pan when first entering Snailcliff, to guide players toward Altaire (the key NPC for forging boss weapons).
[*] Fixed the floating bees bug.
[*] Added a note in the main menu informing players that a staff must be equipped to cast spells.
[*] Added collision to the castle area to prevent players from falling off the map (shoutout to Peaches for the inspiration).
[*] Fixed weapon buffs so they now properly apply status effects (e.g., fire resins now cause burn, frost resins cause frostbite, etc.).
[/list]

With each update, I can feel the game getting closer and closer to a full experience overhaul. 😊 There’s always a ton of work to be done, but I’ve got some exciting ideas on the backlog—and hopefully, I’ll be able to start drafting new adventures to expand the game even further very soon. notes.title: Sharing the latest developments...
notes.content:
[h1]Sharing the Latest Developments – April Update[/h1]

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44662009/ea1d044baabba8f0706dfb3f9faca2b928b4a50a.png[/img]

Hey everyone!

April has been a month of getting back to work and revisiting many of the game’s core systems — and I have to say, it’s been a really fun and rewarding process. These changes are all part of a bigger push to improve the foundation of the game, paving the way for a better experience in the future.

As many of you know, the current focus is on strengthening the existing core gameplay. That means most of the updates listed below are still in development and won't be immediately available. Still, I’d love to share a look at what’s coming in the future [b]Version 2.0 of Cacildes Adventure[/b]!

[b]• AI Improvements[/b]

The enemy and player code has been rewritten and unified, giving enemies the same rights and capabilities as the player. That means they now have their own inventory, can choose their gear and weapons, and even... [i]jump[/i]!

Yep, enemies can now jump to chase Cacildes when he climbs to hard-to-reach spots. No more standing around helplessly while the hero escapes!

[b]See it in action:[/b]
[previewyoutube=bbNA1I6jWJw;full][/previewyoutube]

[b]• Rethinking and Simplifying Inputs[/b]

In the current version of the game, heavy and light attacks are mapped to separate buttons — but that’s changing. Inputs have been simplified to avoid confusion and create a smoother experience.

[b]Here’s what’s new:[/b]

Light and heavy attacks now share the same button: tap for a light attack, hold for a heavy one.

Sprint and dodge are also mapped to the same button: tap to dodge, hold to sprint (just like in Dark Souls).

Heavy attacks can now be charged — the longer you hold, the more damage you deal!

[b]Check out the new system here:[/b]
[previewyoutube=YxxhPARuD7I;full][/previewyoutube]

[b]• Enhanced Magic, Intuitive Shield Blocking, and Dual-Wielding[/b]

Magic is now way more fun to use! You can combine spells with any other weapon or shield (except bows, which for now are only usable in the right hand).

Spells can be charged like heavy attacks for extra damage

Shields now come with their own light and heavy attack sets — and yes, you can bash enemies with them!

[b]Watch it in action:[/b]
[previewyoutube=zdduTqiUJ5I;full][/previewyoutube]

[b]• New UI – Starting with the Title Screen[/b]

The UI is being redesigned with a focus on accessibility and ease of use with a gamepad. Inputs are clearer, more stylish, and offer better feedback to the player. Also, thanks to a major code refactor, it’ll be much easier to add new options in the future.

[b]Take a peek here:[/b]
[previewyoutube=j50waf2r_dE;full][/previewyoutube]

That’s the current progress toward Version 2.0, which is still a little ways off — but I hope you're as excited about these improvements as I am!

Thanks so much for your continued support! :D

notes.title: Important Announcement
notes.content:
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44662009/3a0628ac500716b876c3e15c080079cc0cd66268.png[/img]

[h1]Cacildes Adventure - Major Development Update for 2025[/h1]

Hello everyone, I hope you're all doing well. :-)

After a few months of reflection on the future of [i]Cacildes Adventure[/i], I have reached a conclusion. The sequel, which already has a fully outlined story from beginning to end, might be better suited as an expansion rather than a completely separate new game.

[b]Here are some reasons why I believe it's best to keep everything centralized within [i]Cacildes Adventure 1[/i]:
[/b]

- When I started developing [i]Cacildes Adventure 2[/i], I found myself improving several systems from [i]Cacildes Adventure 1[/i], from UI enhancements to a complete implementation of dual wielding for combat. Seeing these improvements happen in the sequel without being able to bring them into [i]Cacildes Adventure 1[/i] started to create some mental friction, to be honest.

- As a programmer and creator of a product, it would be very difficult to maintain two separate projects. If bug fixes were needed for [i]Cacildes Adventure 1[/i], I would have to go back to a different codebase than the one I'm currently working on and then update the other codebase as well.

- For players who have already purchased [i]Cacildes Adventure 1[/i], I believe it would be much more beneficial to continue receiving updates for this game, which, in my humble opinion, still has plenty of room for improvement at all levels!

For these reasons, I have been considering returning to active development of [i]Cacildes Adventure 1[/i]. My plan is to keep improving it so that in your next playthrough, you'll experience a better game. New players will also benefit from a more polished and continuously improving experience.

I believe the best decision is to pause the sequel, enhance [i]Cacildes Adventure 1[/i], and eventually release a version 2.0 of the game with all the planned improvements (and there are many). After that, I will begin the development of what was going to be [i]Cacildes Adventure 2[/i], but this time as an expansion for [i]Cacildes Adventure 1[/i].

That said, development is resuming for [i]Cacildes Adventure 1[/i], and these are the planned improvements for the first half of 2025:

[h2]Inventory Improvements[/h2]

[b]Item IDs:[/b] Currently, it's not possible to have duplicate weapons/armor or equipment because items do not have unique IDs. For dual wielding to work, it must be possible to have the same weapon twice in the inventory. It would also be great to collect duplicate weapons—whether for selling or for future customization with a weapon modification system (like Bloodstones in [i]Bloodborne[/i] or infusions in [i]Dark Souls 2[/i]). Having unique IDs will allow for all of this.

[b]Shared Items Between the Player and AI:[/b]

As with many other systems in the game, items currently have two versions—one for the player and another for enemies. In reality, the concept of items doesn’t truly exist for enemies. When they use a health potion, it's simply a graphic of a potion with code that restores their health.

Now, a potion used by the player will be the same potion used by the AI. This means the AI will have its own inventory, and all the items available to the player will also be usable by enemies.

[b]Why does this improve the game?[/b] It's much more immersive and fun if an enemy has access to the same equipment and items as the player. If I defeat an enemy with too much health and discover that they were wearing a ring that increases their HP, I can take their ring.

It also saves me work as a developer—by creating an item once and using the same code for both the player and enemies, fewer bugs will occur.

[h2]Combat Improvements[/h2]

This same logic of item sharing will apply to weapons, spells, and even armor. If we defeat an enemy, we can take their weapon, armor, etc.

[b]Boss weapons[/b] will no longer have two versions (one for the player, one for the boss). From now on, there will be only one version—if we defeat the boss, we directly obtain their weapon.

[b]Spells[/b] will also be shared between AI and the player, as well as equipment. If an enemy can use an ability, we can use it too, and vice versa. That will be the philosophy from now on!

[b]Dual wielding[/b] will be fully implemented, along with the ability to equip shields in both hands.

[b]Archery mechanics[/b] will be significantly improved.

The current [b]card system[/b] will be replaced with a [b]skill system[/b], similar to [i]Elden Ring’s Ashes of War[/i]. Skills will vary and may be contextual depending on the equipped weapon.

[b]Blocking and parrying[/b] might become equipable skills, but this is still under consideration.

[h2]UI Improvements[/h2]

The UI will be redesigned to be more accessible for gamepads and visually enhanced using the [b]Synty Fantasy HUD Pack[/b] ([url]https://syntystore.com/products/interface-fantasy-warrior-hud[/url]).

A highly requested feature: [b]dynamic gamepad icons.[/b] If you're using an Xbox controller, you'll see Xbox icons; if you're using a PS4 controller, you'll see PS4 icons.

[h2]Story Improvements[/h2]

I'm considering making the introductory quest involving the chickens optional, allowing players to start the game and roam freely. I believe this would be great for players so they aren't locked out of the entire game until they complete the first quest.

A [b]quest system[/b] is also planned but will likely come later this year. My plan is to add better quest descriptions and a way to track the next destination for players who prefer more guidance—this will be implemented alongside a [b]compass system[/b].

I also have plans to improve dialogue by keeping it external to Unity using [b]JSON files[/b]. I believe this could significantly improve the writing and make it easier to add more dialogue options. Honestly, working within the Unity Editor for dialogues (or any text, really) is a terrible development experience.

[h2]Final Thoughts & Community Involvement[/h2]

The game may not receive updates for a while, but that's okay—the current version is likely stable enough that you can enjoy playing without any major issues!

These are the planned improvements for the 2025 roadmap. Without revealing too much for now, I hope these updates are exciting for you, and I look forward to your enthusiasm!

To stay up to date, I invite you to join the game's Discord server!
[b]➡ [url]https://discord.com/invite/JwnZMc27D2[/url][/b]

Feel free to suggest improvements you'd like to see—this is the best time to do so, as the game will be going through major changes. :-)

Thank you all for your support!

[h3]Update: [/h3]

I've setup a sort of blog / thread where I will be posting the development progress for version 2.0. Please check here:
https://steamcommunity.com/app/2617740/discussions/0/591767767138451473/

Thank you !

[h1]Welcome to the Veilglades[/h1]

Exciting to announce that the second expansion of Cacilde's Adventure is finally out!

After Cacilde finds a mysterious shipmaster in Mountainpass, he is warned not to sail to the Veilglade Peninsula. So naturally, that's what he does...

Explore vampiric crypts, underwater universities and even a sky city! New weapons and gear await, with new swords, double swords, throwable javelins and even a hunting rifle. And best of all, it's free for owners of the base game!

So tag along! Hope you have a grand time exploring this new expansion. ːsteamhappyː

Hey everyone! Busy week with tons of bug fixes and UI improvements. So here's the list!

[u][b]Additions[/b][/u]

- Changed Weight Indicator in UI to be green for lighter equipments, and red for heavier ones

- Enemies no longer collide with player when they die. Previously, they could block doorways and lock player inside certain areas.

- Adjusted status effect logic so that when a player is inflicted, the applied amount equals the base resistance only, ignoring any resistance bonuses. Previously, equipping a resistance ring would cause the status effect bar to grow larger, making the negative effect last longer. Now, it applies only to the base amount, ensuring higher resistance has no drawbacks.

- Made status effect indicator of enemies larger, to better display what status are being applied during battle

- Made the negative status effects applied to the player more noticeable by adding a new HUD indicator. The indicator flashes on the screen once the bar is filled and the status effect activates.

[u][b]Bugfixes[/b][/u]

- Fixed the issue of lost gold appearing in inaccessible locations. Previously, the coins would respawn exactly at the player’s death position, which in some cases resulted in them spawning underwater. Now, the coins are placed at the last grounded position before the player's death, ensuring they respawn in an accessible location.

- Fixed Credits screen not appearing on Title Screen

- Made shop doors in Arun Village not collide with player. This is to avoid that players get locked inside shops if the store closes because of night time.

- Fixed poise displaying wrong values when hovering over equipment

- Fixed Martin dialogue not triggering after opening his cell in Mountainpass

- Fixed poison and blood resin not applying damage to enemies

- Fixed Hugo not attacking the bear due to the stopping distance being too low

That's it for this week! Enjoy this new update :-D

Ultra… eh, depends on the map).

NPCs now react to your progress in the world, with shops giving discounts for completing quests.

But that’s not all - I’m introducing two new weapons and some fresh gear, along with a handful of new consumables. :D 

I hope this huge update stabilizes the game even further. It’s very hard to QA everything as the game is growing with each update, so please keep reporting any bugs or weird issues you may come across! :-)

Hey there, everyone! 😊 I'm very excited about the game officially entering its early access phase. As players embark on their journey as Cacildes, there are already some unexpected errors that need addressing.

One particularly troublesome issue, which was kindly reported by Zaxtor99 (huge shoutout!), involved a frustrating black screen that left players stuck whenever a critical error occurred in the code.

To tackle this head-on and provide you with more feedback, I've implemented a handy error reporting tool. Now, when a critical error arises, you'll see a helpful popup with three options:

- Reload the game to the previous saved state;
- Copy the error and its stack trace to your clipboard - this makes it easier to share the error details for me to troubleshoot it;
- Send an email with the error details - this makes the errors filled out and ready to be sent directly to my inbox, so I can address them right away.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44662009/f23120c1adad63bab6a4acfa30c46961b82ae31f.png[/img]
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44662009/dc3f6b754d69b421ccfca1261d13f27208b7b712.png[/img]

I believe this tool will greatly enhance your gameplay experience!

In addition, I've addressed some other minor issues, including:

- Ensuring companions no longer disappear when you rest on bonfires.
- Fixing minor glitches related to consuming certain items, such as coin purses.
- Removing an annoying message about the inability to block while in two-hand mode.

While this update wasn't originally part of the plan, the discovery of the black screen bug demanded immediate attention. I'm confident that these adjustments will make your gaming experience smoother and more enjoyable.

As always, please don't hesitate to report any incidents you encounter. Your feedback is incredibly valuable in making the game better.

Thank you for playing, and until the next update!

notes.title: Demo - Update #2
notes.content:
Hello everyone! It's been an exciting week with the steam next fest going on. I've had the chance to watch some people play the game and decided to update the demo based on the feedback I received.

[b]Improvements:[/b]
- Added tutorial hints outside Cacildes house. Many player are having difficulty learning the jump key, so I've addressed it with a tutorial.
- Fixed several bugs with the arena mini-game, like wolves spawning right at the center of the arena, or being stuck
- Added smooth animations to the main menu and the dialogue windows, it should improve the overall aspect of the UI
- Replaced many UI sounds

That's a short, but sweet one! 

As always, thanks for playing!

notes.title: Demo update
notes.content:
Hello everyone! Following the demo release, there's been some bugs found and some things I noticed whilst watching many people play.

Here's the full changelog:

[b]Bug Fixes:[/b]

- Fixed a bug with Forest Wanderer Kyle - his dialogue was not triggering;
- Resolved the issue of duplicate dialogue with Dale, the one-armed forest wanderer;
- Fixed a bug where respawning at Bear Cavern map after dying during the boss battle - the fog wall was still active after reloading, preventing the player from reentering the area;
- Improved hitboxes for Cacilde's unarmed attacks
- Addressed the issue where UI elements overlapped, making the watch menu visible and interactable while sitting at a bonfire
- Fixed a bug where equipped weapons didn't display the "equipped" label when reloading
- Corrected distortion in the damage received label on the player
- Fixed a bug where slimes would dodge and not reappear on the surface
- Confetti trap didn't work on the bear, it's fixed now
- Fixed a bug where if we attacked and at the same time rested at a bonfire, it would make the player freeze in the attack animation
- Added control instructions near Cacilde's bed to show right away how to jump :')
- Moved the iron axe to be right outside Cacildes house, making it easy to find a weapon early on
- Improved the fog and visuals in many scenes


[b]New Additions:[/b]

- Added a tutorial section to the main menu, providing an overview of core game mechanics to enhance player understanding
- Included an indicator in the dialogue window to guide players on how to speed up and continue dialogue.


Hope this batch of bugfixes helps having a more enjoyable gameplaye experience. Thank you for playing!
